```{r}
cereals <- read.csv("Cereals.csv")
dim(cereals)
summary(cereals)
```

```{r}
cereals_clean <- na.omit(cereals)
dim(cereals_clean)
```

```{r}
cereal_numeric <- cereals_clean[
   , sapply(cereals_clean, is.numeric)
]

cereals_scaled <- scale(cereal_numeric)
head(cereals_scaled)
```

```{r}
# Euclidean Distance
d <- dist(cereals_scaled, method = "euclidean")
```

```{r}
library(cluster)

hc_single <- agnes(d, method ="single")
hc_complete <- agnes(d, method ="complete")
hc_average <- agnes(d, method ="average")
hc_ward <- agnes(d, method ="ward")

```

```{r}
hc_single$ac
hc_complete$ac
hc_average$ac
hc_ward$ac
```
so Ward is the best method that should be used.

```{r}
pltree(hc_single, main = "Single Linkage")
pltree(hc_complete, main = "Complete Linkage")
pltree(hc_average, main = "Average Linkage")
pltree(hc_ward, main = "Ward's Method")
```
I would choose the ward method because it has the highest coefficient 0.9046042

```{r}
clusters <- cutree(hc_ward, k= 3)
table(clusters)
```

```{r}
pltree(hc_ward, main = "Ward's Method - 3 Clusters")
rect.hclust(hc_ward, k = 3, border = 2:4)
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)
n <- nrow(cereals_scaled)
index_A <- sample(1:n, size = floor(n/2))

A <- cereals_scaled[index_A, ]
B <- cereals_scaled[-index_A, ]

nrow(A)
nrow(B)
```

```{r}
d_A <- dist(A, method = "euclidean")

hc_A <- agnes(d_A, method = "ward")

clusters_A <- cutree(as.hclust(hc_A), k =3)

table(clusters_A)
```

```{r}
centroids <- aggregate(A,
                       by = list(cluster = clusters_A),
                       FUN = mean)

centroids
```


```{r}
centroids_values <- as.matrix(centroids[, -1])

predicted_B <- rep(NA, nrow(B))
for (i in 1:nrow(B)) {
distances <- apply(centroids_values, 1, function(center) {
  sqrt(sum((B[i, ] - center)^2))
})
  predicted_B[i] <- which.min(distances)
}

table(predicted_B)
```

```{r}
original_B <- clusters[-index_A]
table(Original = original_B,
      predicted = predicted_B)
```

```{r}
aggregate(cereal_numeric, 
          by = list(cluster = clusters),
          FUN = mean)
```

```{r}
cereal_nutrition <- cereal_numeric[, c(
  "calories", "protein", "fat", "sodium",
  "fiber", "carbo", "sugars", "potass",
  "vitamins"
)]
cereal_nutrition_scaled <- scale(cereal_nutrition)
```

```{r}
d_nutrition <- dist(cereal_nutrition_scaled, method = "euclidean")
hc_nutrition <- agnes(d_nutrition, method = "ward")
pltree(hc_nutrition, main = "Ward's Method - Healthy Cereals")
```

```{r}
clusters_nutrition <- cutree(as.hclust(hc_nutrition), k =3)
table(clusters_nutrition)

aggregate(cereal_nutrition, 
          by = list(cluster = clusters_nutrition),
          FUN = mean)
```

```{r}
data.frame(
  name = cereals_clean$name,
  cluster = clusters_nutrition
  )
```
I would recommend cluster 1 because it has cereal with high protein and fiber and less calories and sugar
